data: Do all five blue lines in Figure 2 show an increase in log-likelihood (scaled by 10e+07) as the number of iterations increases?

The question asks whether all five blue lines in Figure 2 show an increase in log-likelihood as the number of iterations increases. From the analysis of the key visual elements, we can see that each line represents a different domain and is colored blue. The x-axis represents the number of iterations, and the y-axis represents the log-likelihood scaled by 10e+07. 

By examining the graph, we can observe that for each domain, the blue line starts at a lower value on the y-axis and increases as the number of iterations increases. This trend is consistent across all five domains. Therefore, it appears that all five blue lines show an increase in log-likelihood as the number of iterations increases.
